_schema.subject: server/watch/relay.py turn_local_to_vector_events + NudgePolicy (phone turn -> watch nudge)
_schema.description: Golden test vectors for the phone->watch tone-escalation relay (Track 1, 2026-08-24). Each case constructs one fresh NudgePolicy from `config`, then feeds `inputs` in order — one relay call per step — and asserts `expected[i]` after step i. This file is deliberately SEPARATE from nudge_policy.json: that file's `inputs.events` are already-levelled vector observations, while these inputs are raw phone turns (tone scores + loudness) that the relay must first turn into events. Same conventions otherwise (README.md): plain field names, seconds as floats, fresh instance per case.

config.cooldown_s: float — passed straight to NudgePolicy (see nudge_policy.json)
config.channels: list of channel labels, as nudge_policy.json
config.subscriptions: list of {vector, sensitivity, haptics, channel}, as nudge_policy.json — cases use the account defaults (yelling + aggressive_tone on A, sensitivity 1.0, haptics on)
config.baseline_rms_db: float or null — the wearer's ENROLLMENT loudness baseline in dBFS (EnrollmentBaseline.rms_db). null means 'not enrolled and no prior phone turns yet', i.e. loudness can't be measured and never yells (the relay's live running-median fallback is NOT exercised by this file; it's covered by test_relay.py)

inputs.t: float seconds — the watch session's stream clock at relay time (relay uses engine.t, never the phone's turn timestamps)

turn.is_self: true | false | null — the phone's voiceprint verdict (TurnLocalEvent.is_self). ONLY true produces events; false (another speaker) and null (unknown) are ignored outright
turn.rms_dbfs: float or null — TurnLocalEvent.prosody.rms_dbfs; null = not measured (never 0). Loudness level = YELLING_LEVELS over `rms_dbfs - baseline_rms_db` (>=14 -> 3, >=10 -> 2, >=6 -> 1), and anything <= -45 dBFS (SILENCE_FLOOR_DBFS) is noise floor, not loudness
turn.text_tone: {frustration, defensiveness} (0-100 ints, either may be null/absent) or null — TurnLocalEvent.text_tone
turn.tone_flag: {scores: {frustration?, defensiveness?} (0-100 floats), confidence: 0..1} or null — an optional ToneFlagEvent relayed alongside; ignored below TONE_FLAG_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.5)

_schema.tone_levels: max(frustration, defensiveness) over BOTH tone sources -> level: >=85 -> 3, >=70 -> 2, >=55 -> 1, else 0 (relay.py TONE_LEVELS). Rides the `aggressive_tone` vector

expected.events: list of {vector, level} the relay converted this turn into, in emission order (yelling first, then aggressive_tone); [] when nothing cleared a first rung — and an empty relay does NOT tick the policy (no cooldown de-escalation from phone cadence)
expected.nudges: list of {channel, level, vectors} emitted by the policy for this step, as nudge_policy.json
expected.levels: map channel -> current level after this step, as nudge_policy.json

applies_to.server: the Python relay (server/watch/relay.py) — every case. No watch/phone port exists yet: the watch never sees tone, and the phone's own coaching path has no wrist to nudge

cases.name: calm_volume_hostile_tone_escalates
cases.description: The case the relay exists for: a self turn at exactly baseline loudness (0 dB over -> no yelling) but with frustration 78 (>= 70 -> level 2) raises channel A to 2 on the tone lane alone.

cases.name: other_speaker_hostile_turn_is_ignored
cases.description: Bias guard: the OTHER party's furious turn (is_self false, frustration 95, 20 dB over) produces nothing — the watch measures its wearer, never the person they're talking to.

cases.name: unknown_speaker_is_ignored
cases.description: is_self null (no enrolled voiceprint to match against) is not evidence about the wearer: identical hostile content, still nothing.

cases.name: tone_threshold_rungs
cases.description: Pins every TONE_LEVELS rung: 54 is under the first bar (nothing — and no policy tick), 55 -> 1, 70 -> 2, 85 -> 3, each a fresh escalation that emits. Loudness is at baseline throughout so only the tone lane moves. Uses defensiveness for the middle rung to pin that both keys count.

cases.name: db_and_tone_combine_as_max
cases.description: Both lanes fire on one turn: 16 dB over (yelling 3) with frustration 60 (tone 1) -> the channel takes the max, 3, and `vectors` names only the winner. The next turn is calm-volume but defensiveness 90 (tone 3) — equal to the current level, so it sustains (refreshes the clock) without re-emitting. A third, genuinely calm turn produces no events and therefore no policy tick: the level holds at 3 even though 30 s > cooldown have passed on the relay's clock (the watch's own windows own de-escalation).

cases.name: db_lane_alone_matches_watch_ladder
cases.description: With no tone data at all, the phone's loudness walks the SAME +6/+10/+14 ladder the watch mic uses: -23.9 (6.1 over) -> 1, -20 (10 over) -> 2, -16 (14 over) -> 3.

cases.name: tone_flag_counts_only_when_confident
cases.description: A server ToneFlagEvent (audio tone) with frustration 90 at confidence 0.9 raises level 3 with no text tone at all; the same scores at confidence 0.3 are an observation, not a verdict, and produce nothing.

cases.name: two_tone_sources_take_the_max
cases.description: Text tone says 60 (level 1), the audio ToneFlagEvent says defensiveness 72 (level 2) at confidence 0.8 -> the louder source wins: level 2.

cases.name: missing_measurements_are_not_zero
cases.description: Honest degradation: no prosody, no tone, no flag -> nothing to say. And a turn at the silence floor (-50 dBFS, 20 dB UNDER baseline) with no tone is noise floor, not loudness. Neither step ticks the policy.

cases.name: no_baseline_means_loudness_cannot_be_measured
cases.description: baseline_rms_db null (not enrolled, no prior phone turns): a -10 dBFS turn is loud in absolute terms but there is nothing to compare it to, so it never yells — the tone lane still works (frustration 70 -> 2). Absolute thresholds are exactly what the bias guard forbids.

cases.name: tone_lane_respects_haptics_off_subscription
cases.description: The tone lane is an ordinary aggressive_tone subscription: a wearer who switched that vector's haptics off gets no tone nudge (frustration 95) while a loud turn (16 dB over) still nudges on yelling. Settings, not the relay, own the final say.
